subject: Post-demo: FinTechCo performance/SLO checklist and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Nina Patel <nina@fintechco.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo: FinTechCo performance/SLO checklist and next steps
Attachments: FinTechCo_SLO_checklist_v1.pdf

Hi Alex / Nina —

Thanks again for taking the time today to walk through the demo and the live load test. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture the performance/SLO items we discussed and propose next steps so we can get you a realistic baseline and MAP (mutual action plan).

Quick recap of FinTechCo targets you mentioned:
- P95 latency target: <= 200 ms for short customer-facing prompts (~75 tokens)
- Sustained throughput: ~500 requests/sec during peak windows
- Concurrency: ability to handle ~50 concurrent interactive streams (may spike to 100 for batch jobs)
- Streaming: token-level streaming for interactive UI (low-latency incremental responses)
- SLA/availability expectation: 99.9% for production endpoints

Proposed MAP items (high level):
1) You provide a representative sample workload and top 10 prompt templates + average token distribution.
2) We provision a test environment (sandbox API key + dedicated test capacity) and run a 2-hour sustained throughput test (500 rps) and a 30-minute spike test to 1k rps.
3) Redwood provides: SLO checklist, perf run logs, and recommended config (batching, instance types, model variant, quantization options).
4) Joint review call to go over results and decide next steps (Dedicated vs Hosted and pricing).

Questions from our side for the perf run:
- Do you need token-level streaming with partial-reply commit semantics, or will line-by-line streaming suffice?
- Are there any PII/PCI rules for test data we should be aware of?
- Do you have an internal SLA/uptime target beyond 99.9% for legal?

Next steps: I can set up the sandbox and schedule the perf run as early as Wed May 12. If that works for you, please send the sample workload and confirm whether streaming needs to be token-level.

Attaching the SLO checklist I mentioned.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Subject: Re: Post-demo: FinTechCo performance/SLO checklist and next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple clarifications from our side: 

1) Streaming: We do need token-level streaming for the customer chat UI (we render as tokens arrive). Line-by-line won't be sufficient for the top-level experience.
2) Concurrency: Our initial conservative target is 50 concurrent interactive streams, but during batch analytics runs we occasionally push to ~120 concurrent inference sessions. We need to understand graceful degradation behavior for those spikes.
3) Data/privacy: For the perf run we'll strip PHI/PCI from samples; procurement will want a short statement on data handling during the run.

Can you confirm the test environment isolation (sandbox keys + logs accessible to our infra team)? Also — could you share an estimate ballpark for Dedicated capacity pricing for the config you expect? We need that for internal procurement.

Best,
Alex
Head of Engineering, FinTechCo
alex.johnson@fintechco.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Nina Patel <nina@fintechco.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Post-demo: FinTechCo performance/SLO checklist and next steps
Attachments: perf_run_logs_20270511.zip

Alex — great, thanks for the clarifications. Short answers:

- Token-level streaming: confirmed. We'll enable token streaming on the sandbox endpoints for the interactive tests so you can validate rendering latency and partial output behavior.
- Concurrency/spikes: we'll run both sustained (500 rps, ~50 concurrency) and burst tests (to 1k rps / up to 120 concurrency) to observe tail latency and degradation modes. We'll also capture KV cache hit/miss stats so we can recommend caching to reduce cost.
- Sandbox isolation: sandbox keys are isolated from production; logs will be accessible to your infra team via a temporary read-only link (we'll share with procurement/infra). We'll include a one-page data handling statement for the perf run.

Attached are the initial perf run logs from our staging run (sanitized) and an updated SLO checklist with fields we can populate together.

Proposed timeline:
- Tue May 11: provisioning + sandbox key 
- Wed May 12: 10:00 PT perf run (2-hour sustained + 30-minute spike)
- Thu May 13: 09:00 PT joint review call to go over results

If that schedule works I will: 1) provision the test key and share the read-only logs link, 2) run the tests, and 3) send the perf run archive and a preliminary recommendation doc.

Also: regarding Dedicated pricing, I'll loop in Marcus with a short note below for a ballpark and we can follow up with a formal sheet.

Thanks — Marissa

---

> Attached are the initial perf run logs from our staging run (sanitized) and an updated SLO checklist with fields we can populate together.

Recommended config (from infra):
- Model variant: rwd-13b-q4f (good latency/cost tradeoff)
- Instance suggestion: 4x A100-80GB or equivalent pinned Dedicated slots for sustained 500 rps tests
- Batching: dynamic batching with max batch size 64 for low latency
- KV caching: enable prefix caching for repeated prompt headers (could cut tokens served by ~25%)
- Quantization: q4f recommended for production; bring q8_0 for internal cost comparison runs

Metrics we'll capture during run: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU util, batch sizes, KV cache hit rate, memory pressure, and streaming latency (time to first token).

If procurement wants a short note on data handling, we will provide a one-page statement confirming sanitized test data, sandbox isolation, and log access limited to named FinTechCo users.

Thanks,
Ethan
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
